title: Facial asymmetry in unicoronal craniosynostosis: automated three-dimensional quantification of surgical outcomes
html: Craniosynostosis is the premature closure of one or more cranial sutures which may result in functional and aesthetic complications. Non-syndromic unicoronal craniosynostosis commonly leads to facial asymmetry. This study aimed to quantify changes in facial asymmetry before and after surgical treatment using an automated 3D technique. A retrospective study was performed including 32 patients treated at Radboud University Medical Center Nijmegen between 2011 and 2024. Pre- and postoperative three-dimensional facial photographs were analysed, and asymmetry was quantified using regional root-mean-square (RMS) values.
